title: Usage credit lifecycle and tiered rate consolidator
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We need a single service that materializes customer usage credits across multiple ingestion windows and maps them into the correct tiered rate buckets for billing and console display. Current downstream pipelines apply ad-hoc prorations and windowing that produce inconsistent per-tenant effective rates when requests span multiple routes, model variants, or token price changes. This ticket defines a consolidator service that performs deterministic credit lifecycle processing: (1) consumable credit decay and window stitching for late-arriving events; (2) deterministic tier assignment for mixed-rate usage; (3) an auditable mapping of raw usage rows to effective billing units suitable for invoicing and console breakdowns.
acceptance_criteria: All tenant usage that arrives within a 7-day lateness window is deterministically attributed to a single billing unit with a stable effective rate
Service emits records compatible with existing billing join keys (tenant_id, billing_period, effective_rate_id, usage_unit_id) and passes downstream schema validation
End-to-end pipeline produces <0.1% variance in per-tenant monthly spend compared to a golden retrospective recalculation for a 30-day test corpus
Console shows per-route and per-model breakdowns that sum to invoiced totals with margin of error < $0.50 per tenant for test tenants
Backfill job completes for 90 days of historical data within acceptable cluster resources and produces a diff report highlighting changes vs previous reconciler
implementation_notes: Introduce a credit lifecycle finite-state model with phases: incoming, buffered, decayed, allocated, finalized
Use a deterministic tie-breaker for events with identical timestamps: (source_priority, request_id) to ensure idempotent attribution
Leverage existing event avro schema; extend with effective_rate_id and allocation_trace fields (strings) for downstream auditing
Expose a small HTTP health and metrics endpoint for rollout; metrics must include allocations_per_second, reassignments_count, and late_arrivals_count
Design for eventual single-writer per tenant-per-period by sharding on tenant_id hash to maintain linearizability of allocation decisions
steps: Design spec and data contract review with Billing PM and Console PM
Prototype allocation algorithm in a Spark job against a 30-day sample corpus
Implement gRPC-backed consolidator service that consumes the normalized usage topic
Add schema extensions and validators to pipeline, include backward-compat checks
Create backfill controller to run reprocessing on historical partitions with dry-run diff
Add end-to-end tests and a small canary run for 50 tenants before full rollout
Roll out with feature flag and monitor console diffs and alert thresholds
